title.narrative: People’s Republic of China Support To UN-Habitat through the Bangkok Programme Office - People's Republic of China and UN-Habitat Cooperation For The Implementation Of The SDGs and NUA in the Asia-Pacific

description.narrative:
Since 2010, UN-Habitat has sought to strengthen the collaboration with the UN Economic and Social Commission of Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) in Bangkok. UN-Habitat’s Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, established in Fukuoka, Japan since 1997 established a Programmes Offices in Bangkok in 2010. The office was instrumental in strengthening the mainly normative and capacity building collaboration with ESCAP, especially with the Sustainable Urban Development Section under the Environment and Development Division.
To date, this collaboration yielded significant results: - Flagship publications on the state of cities in Asia-Pacific (2011, 2015, 2019, planned 2023); - Co-hosting of major urban forums in Asia-Pacific, e.g. APUF6 (back-to-back with the Habitat III Regional Meeting, 2015), APUF7 (Penang, 2008), APUF8 (planned in Suwon, 2023); - Joint capacity building of urban leaders, e.g. the Asia-Pacific Mayors Academy, since 2019; - Joint policy advisory services, e.g. on localizing SDGs and Voluntary Local Reviews; - Joint events in support of the regional review and reporting of the implementation of the SDGs and the New Urban Agenda, including through the yearly Asia-Pacific Forum for Sustainable Development.
Given budgetary restrictions in recent years, UN-Habitat’s collaboration with ESCAP has fully delivered by the Regional Representative and senior professional staff based in Fukuoka. P4 and P5 posts in Bangkok were frozen. At a formal level, the Regional Representative, at D1 director level, still collaborates with the Director of the Environment and Development Division.
Thus, this proposal will commence a new collaboration of UN-Habitat through the Bangkok Programme Office with the Government of China through the Ministry of Housing and Urban Development.
The new collaboration will address a key challenge of the Bangkok Programme Office, by providing soft-earmarked resources towards its optimal collaboration with ESCAP and the RPC/PRG, while at the time leveraging these collaborations towards the improved dissemination of the Shanghai Award and Shanghai Adapted Index and strengthened capacity building of developing countries.
The Bangkok Programme Office will continue to build out its MCO role with earmarked project resources and core funding as available, as guided by the Executive Director and the governing bodies of UN-Habitat. However, the collaboration with the Government of China and its soft-earmarked contributions will be applied to strengthen the regional UN system support functions of UN-Habitat.
To optimize the new collaboration, the Bangkok Programmes Office will collaborate with Chinese official institutions, programmes and initiatives, including the Belt and Road International Cooperation. This collaboration will be done with the guidance of UN-Habitat Headquarters as needed, under the supervision of the ROAP and in collaboration with UN-Habitat’s staff and offices in China.
The collaboration is established for a timeframe of 3 years, which includes an inception phase of 9 months required for the recruitment process of the expert resource (P-staff). As per UN rules and regulations, the collaboration and the detailed budget is established on the basis of agreed earmarked funding, paid or committed in writing.
Provided sufficient earmarked funding is available or committed in writing, the collaboration will be automatically extended, by increments of 3 years. The collaboration can also be terminated at the first applicable end date by either Party if so, requested in writing with prior notice of 3 months.
This new collaboration will yield the following outcomes: - Improved intergovernmental communication of UN-Habitat with the UN system-wide entities in Bangkok - Enhanced publicity and dissemination, regionally and globally, of the Shanghai Award and the UMF-Shanghai Adapted Index, in collaboration with UN-Habitat’s SDG Cities flagship programme - Increased capacity building for developing countries, regionally and globally, on the implementation of the UN Agenda 2030 and the New Urban Agenda.
